spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation

**¶1:**
What is Divine Love itself? [GAP-1: the spiritual definition or essence that initiates the inquiry] [GAP-2: a further unfolding of that essence, likely how it is perceived or received] each [GAP-3: state of spiritual life, or each being that partakes of it], recognizing it as 'Divine Love.'

**¶2:**
Divine Love is the Divine Itself, the Infinite Source of all good, which abides in its own celestial kingdom. The whole of the Divine nature is made manifest within that kingdom. These two are one indivisible life: the Divine Itself and its Love — for the Divine Esse and Divine Love are not two but one. Because the Divine has given itself forth into all things through its proceeding, as it exists within its own infinite states of being, therefore they recognized the Divine, the Lord of all that exists, as Love Itself. For it has granted dominion and life to all its proceeding states and to all that is conjoined with it as its very members.

**¶4:**
What, conversely, is the opposite of Divine Love? Hatred is the primal spiritual death that welled up from the proprium. It brought into manifestation the entire realm of falsity and evil. It is called abomination because it has consumed and destroyed all the offspring of its own perdition; yet it assaulted even that Divine Good which is utterly foreign and apart from it, and profaned it. Therefore they call it the abominated — for it has wrought devastation both within the natural will, and upon what does not belong to it: the Divine things it invaded and corrupted.

**¶5:**
Even now this self-love and falsity from evil continues to bring devastation and ruin upon every natural will. It extinguishes spiritual life through manifold forms of spiritual death — those that are made evident in every state of existence and in every kind of being. Even the Divine Truth in its suffering — the living good held captive within the human spirit — this evil likewise profanes and extinguishes, just as it did from the very origin of the fall. Therefore they recognize it as the abomination proceeding from the abomination, the self-love born of self-love, the infernal issuing from the infernal, the evil that comes forth from evil in unbroken hereditary succession.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: What is love? [Love is the Father.][He has been revealed to] each [aeon], calling it 'love'.

Love is the Father of Greatness, who dwells in his glorious land. The entirety of the divine has been revealed [there]in! These two are a single living body, the Father and his love; because he has given himself for every thing, as he exists in his aeons. Indeed, due to this, they called the Father, the Lord of the totality, 'love'. For he gave the victory to his aeons and his limbs.

What, conversely, is hate? Hate is the first death that welled up. It revealed the land of Darkness. This one called 'hate', because it has ruined all its perdition's offspring; it sinned even against a power foreign to it, and ruined it. Due to this they shall call it 'hated'; for it has caused destruction, both wounding in flesh, and what is not its own.

Today again it causes wounding and destruction in all flesh. It kills them all with diverse deaths; these that are displayed today in every thing, in every type. Even the Cross of Light, the living soul, likewise too it ruins and kills them; as it did at the start. Indeed, due to this have they called it 'hated', this one from the hated; the envy from the envy; the devil from the devil; the bad that came about from the bad.

fills.explanation: The spiritual reading identifies GAP-1 as "the spiritual definition or essence," and ¶2 elaborates "Love is the Father of Greatness"; this compact thesis statement mirrors the hate parallel ("Hate is the first death") and establishes the identification of Love with the Divine Itself.

The spiritual reading identifies GAP-2 as "how it is perceived or received"; ¶2 uses the same verb ("The entirety of the divine has been revealed [there]in"), and the hate parallel has "It revealed the land of Darkness," establishing revelation as the operative verb in this chapter's framework.

The spiritual reading identifies GAP-3 as "state of spiritual life, or each being that partakes of it"; in the Kephalaia's vocabulary, "aeon" is the precise term for a proceeding state of divine life, and ¶2 confirms: "he exists in his aeons... he gave the victory to his aeons and his limbs."
